sample.task:
Write the third chapter of detailed story with a lot of dialogues, based on this: (2018 Mowgli movie's version of Akela and Dragon Ball Super's version of Android 18 say what they think about it)

The previous chapters were these: [Chapter 1
Once upon a time, in a distant corner of the cosmos, there was a planetoid the size of Jupiter. This colossal celestial body was home to several ancient civilizations, each one unique in its own right and estemmed way of life. What made this planetoide even more peculiar was the fact that thousands of characters from various universes, each with their own abilities and strengths, found themselves inexplicably transported there.
Upon their arrival, the characters discovered that their individual powers varied greatly. While some were as mighty as they had been in their own realms, others found that their strengths had been diminished. To even the scales, many warriors who had once been weaker than others were now endowed with a newfound power that brought them on par with the mightiest heroes and villains.
As time went by, the myriad characters began exploring the vast and diverse landscape of this enigmatic planetoide. While some sought to learn its origin, many others realized that they could increase their own power through effort and dedication, effectively “leveling up” and ultimately surpassing their fellow fighters.
For several months, they traversed the sprawling expanse of the planetoid, challenging and defeating other warriors, as well as forging alliances with those who shared their ideals.
Miles “Tails” Prower, the young two-tailed fox from the Archie Comics universe, had spent countless days exploring the vast landscapes of the planetoid. His engineering skills and intellect had served him well during his adventures, and he had even managed to level up his abilities, growing stronger and smarter each day.
One fateful afternoon, as he delved deep into the forests of the planetoid, Tails stumbled upon a mysterious chamber hidden beneath the roots of an ancient tree. The entrance, though well-hidden, bore the signs of past explorations. Piqued by curiosity, Tails ventured inside.
The chamber was dimly lit by the flickering light of magical torches, revealing dusty shelves filled with scrolls and documents that had been left untouched for eons. As he carefully scanned the room, Tails found one peculiar document that had seemingly fallen on the ground. He unfolded it gently and began to read.
“What’s this? ‘Cloning Experiment Log’?” Tails wondered aloud, his curiosity burning even brighter. As he continued to peruse the document, a terrible truth began to dawn on him. All of the characters transported to this planetoid, himself included, were not the originals, but mere clones of these warriors. The original ones were still living their lives in their respective universes, unaware of the existence of their duplicates on this colossal celestial body.
Tails reeled from this revelation, his world instantly turning upside down. He knew that his friends, as well as their newfound allies, would need to know the truth. He raced back to the makeshift village where Sonic, Knuckles, and the other characters had set up their base of operations.
“Sonic! Knuckles! Guys, I’ve got something important to tell you!” Tails shouted, waving the document as he entered their shared living space.
“What’s up, Tails? You seem more freaked out than usual,” Sonic said, looking up from a map he had been studying closely with Knuckles.
“It’s… it’s this document I found,” Tails panted, catching his breath. “You guys… we’re clones. All of us.”
The room went silent as they all processed the shocking news. Denial was the first reaction, as Knuckles scoffed, “Clones? Seriously, Tails? That’s ridiculous.”
“No, it’s true!” Tails insisted. “I found the logs of the experiments that created us, and according to this, each of us was created here on the planetoid, while our originals live out their lives in our home universes!”
The grim revelation sent shockwaves through every character that eventually find out about this revelation. Some characters were devastated, while others questioned their own existence and purpose.

Chapter 2
“What do you mean we’re clones?” Katsuki Bakugo roared, his voice nearly shaking the makeshift wooden walls around him. The explosive and short-tempered hero from the My Hero Academia universe was not known for his patience, and the frustration that filled the room was palpable.
Across from him, Jiren the Grey – an extraterrestrial who had come from the Dragon Ball Super universe with immense power – narrowed his eyes, studying the document that Tails had brought back. He remained calm and composed, despite the escalating tension that threatened to boil over. “It would seem that we have all been duped,” Jiren said somberly.
Word had spread quickly among the inhabitants of that sumerian village, and the news of their true identities had attracted everyone’s attention. Some heroes and villains alike had gathered in the small common area to discuss the sudden revelation, but most of them could not believe what they had just been told.
“I refuse to believe it!” Bakugo bellowed, his fists igniting with fury. “I have my own dreams and goals in life! I want to become the number one hero in my universe! And now you’re telling me that I’m just a carbon copy?”
“I understand your anger, Bakugo,” Jiren replied, his composure remaining unbroken. “But instead of cursing the darkness, we should light a candle.”
“What are you babbling about, alien?” Bakugo snorted, glaring at Jiren as if he was a mortal enemy.
Jiren sighed and looked around at the diverse crowd that had gathered. “I’m simply saying that we should use this information to our advantage. Perhaps we can find a way to return to our respective universes and confront our original selves.”
“But why?” asked Sonic, who had previously been leaning against a wall with folded arms. “If this is true, then what’s the point of going back? We can’t just replace our originals, and even if we could, what would that make us? Are we just destined to be second-best for the rest of our existence?”
“Who said anything about replacing them, Sonic?” Jiren countered. “But we have the right to know who we are, where we came from, and why we were created.”
“We could also try to find a way to contact our original selves,” Tails suggested hesitantly, his twin tails twitching nervously. “Maybe there’s something they can do to help us. I know it’s a long shot, but it’s worth a try, right?”
The room went silent for a moment, and then Knuckles, who had been standing silently in a corner, spoke up. “You know what? Tails is right. Sure, we’re clones, but we exist. And since we’re here, we might as well make the best of it.”
Bakugo scowled but didn’t say anything. Knuckles continued, “Jiren’s got a point, too. We have to at least try to find out more about our origins and purpose. So, what do you say, everybody? Are we in this together, or are we just going to whine and cry about it?”
His words seemed to stir something within everyone gathered there. Even Bakugo grumbled, “Fine. But don’t think this means I like any of you.”]
sample.chosen:
**Chapter 3**

The makeshift village was abuzz with a new sense of purpose. Characters from various universes, now united under the unexpected revelation, started to strategize their next steps. In the heart of the village, Akela, the wise and battle-hardened wolf from the 2018 Mowgli movie, sat with Android 18 from Dragon Ball Super. They were deep in conversation, reflecting on the recent turn of events.

Akela, his fur streaked with silver, looked at Android 18 with a thoughtful expression. "What do you make of all this, 18? You've seen more of the cosmos than most of us here."

Android 18, leaning against a tree with her arms crossed, shrugged slightly. "It's not the strangest thing I've encountered, but it's up there. I think the key here is to stay focused. We can't change what we are, but we can decide what to do with this information."

Akela nodded, his ears twitching as he listened to the hum of activity around them. "Agreed. But we must also consider the emotional toll this takes on everyone. Some are taking it harder than others."

"You mean like that Bakugo kid?" Android 18 smirked. "He's loud, but he's got spirit. We could use that kind of energy."

Akela chuckled softly. "Indeed. But we need to channel that energy properly. We can't have him blowing up our only chance at finding answers."

Just then, Tails approached them, his eyes filled with determination. "Akela, Android 18, I could use your help. We're organizing teams to scout the planetoid for more information. Would you be willing to lead one?"

Android 18 pushed off from the tree, standing straight. "Count me in. I've got a few ideas on where to look."

Akela stood as well, his eyes gleaming with resolve. "I'll lead a team too. We'll cover more ground that way."

Tails smiled, relieved. "Great! Thank you both. We'll meet back here before nightfall to share what we've found."

As Tails scurried off, Akela turned to Android 18. "Who do you plan to take with you?"

Android 18 looked around, her gaze landing on a few familiar faces. "I think I'll take Goku. He's got a good nose for trouble. And maybe that Naruto kid. He's got a lot of energy too."

Akela nodded approvingly. "Good choices. I'll take Shere Khan and Bagheera. They're formidable trackers and know the ways of the wild better than most."

With their teams decided, Akela and Android 18 set off in different directions, each leading their group into the vast expanse of the planetoid. The landscape varied greatly, from dense forests to arid deserts, each area holding potential clues to their existence.

As Akela's team ventured deeper into the forest, Shere Khan, the powerful tiger, paused and sniffed the air. "There's something unusual nearby," he growled.

Bagheera, the sleek black panther, nodded in agreement. "I sense it too. It's not an animal... more like a machine."

Akela's ears perked up. "Let's investigate. Be on your guard."

Meanwhile, Android 18's team was exploring a rocky terrain filled with strange, towering structures. Goku, with his keen senses, pointed towards one of the structures. "There's something strong in there," he said, his eyes widening with excitement.

Naruto, eager as ever, dashed forward. "Let's check it out!"

As the teams delved deeper into their respective areas, the mystery of the planetoid began to unfold, revealing secrets that would challenge their understanding of themselves and their purpose. The journey was fraught with danger, but with leaders like Akela and Android 18 at the helm, they were ready to face whatever came their way.

Back at the village, Tails waited anxiously, hoping that the scouting teams would return with answers that could shed more light on their existence. The fate of the clones rested on the success of these missions, and the anticipation hung heavy in the air. The stage was set for discoveries that could change their lives forever.

“I don’t know about you guys, but I think we should take this opportunity to learn more about ourselves and our abilities,” Tails said, his voice filled with determination. “We may be clones, but that doesn’t mean we can’t be just as great as our originals.”
“I agree,” Sonic chimed in. “We’ve already proven ourselves to be powerful fighters, and I don’t see why we can’t continue to grow and improve.”
Jiren nodded in agreement. “Indeed. We may have been created for a specific purpose, but that doesn’t mean we can’t exceed those expectations.”
Bakugo rolled his eyes. “Please. You guys are just making excuses for not being able to beat me.”
Sonic smirked. “Oh, I don’t know about that, Bakugo. But I do know that we’re all in this together. And if we work together, we can achieve great things.”
The group fell into a thoughtful silence, each lost in their own thoughts about their newfound identities. It was clear that they all had a lot to process, and the weight of their situation was beginning to sink in.
Finally, Jiren spoke up. “I suggest that we form a council of sorts. A group of representatives from each of our respective universes, tasked with investigating the origins of our existence and finding a way to return home.”
“That’s a great idea,” Tails said, his eyes lighting up with excitement. “We could each choose a representative from our own universe, and then we could work together to uncover the truth.”
Sonic nodded in agreement. “And we could also use this opportunity to learn more about each other’s worlds. I mean, think about it. We’ve got heroes and villains from all sorts of different universes here. We could learn so much from each other.”
Bakugo scoffed. “I don’t need to learn anything from any of you. I’m already the best.”
Sonic grinned. “Is that so? Well, I guess we’ll just have to see about that, won’t we?”
The group laughed, and for a moment, the tension that had been building between them dissipated. They may have been clones, but they were still heroes in their own right. And with each other’s help, they knew that they could overcome any obstacle that stood in their way.
As they began to discuss the logistics of forming a council, Tails couldn’t help but feel a sense of excitement and anticipation. This was a new chapter in their lives, and he knew that they were all going to be a part of something truly special.
